title: NOAA next-day storm probabilities had excess G1 and G2 totals but no clear G3 excess on 816 days in 2023-2025
abstract: We tested NOAA planetary geomagnetic storm probabilities against definitive GFZ daily maximum Kp on available target dates in 2023-2025. The primary next-day strong-to-extreme (G3+) test gave 29.45 expected event days and 29 observed on 816 dates. Mean probability minus outcome was 0.055 percentage points, with 95% 27-day block limits of -1.08 to +1.11. This does not prove conditional calibration. Secondary G1+ and G2+ sums were 235.76 versus 157 and 94.45 versus 59, with mean errors of +9.65 and +4.34 points. The lower-level excess remains with strict numerical Kp thresholds and with NOAA estimated planetary outcomes. A day-3 G3+ deficit depends on the threshold definition. We preserve the NOAA source snapshot, source hashes, code, aggregate evidence and an independent parser check. Archive gaps, only three years, few severe event days, index differences and block assumptions limit inference. This is a severity-specific verification result, not evidence of one common bias in all public hazard products.

display.caption: Mean issued probabilities and observed daily frequencies for each lead and severity. Outcomes use rounded definitive GFZ Kp levels. Sample sizes are 816, 815 and 814 dates. Vertical scales differ by severity.
